chunks: And from him, from Abu Jamilah, from Sulayman ibn Harun, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Whoever drinks from the water of the Euphrates and is moistened with it, he is among those who love us, the Ahl al-Bayt.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The Ahl al-Bayt (Family of the Prophet)
key_terms.حُنِّكَ بِهِ: Moistened with it (referring to the ritual of putting sweetened water in a newborn's mouth)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of drinking from the Euphrates River in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking the physical act of drinking from the Euphrates—a river blessed in Islamic tradition—to spiritual affinity with the Ahl al-Bayt. This hadith highlights the Euphrates as a symbol of divine sustenance and purity, suggesting that consuming its water serves as a tangible sign of love and allegiance to the Prophet's household.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, (from Ibn Faďďāl), from Abī Jamīlah (Mufaďďal ibn Sāliḥ Al-Usdi), from Sulaymān ibn Hārūn, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
If the water of the Euphrates River is used to open the mouth of a (newborn baby) and is his first drink, he will be among those who love us, the Ahlul Bayt.
